resources.string: Smart battery and system monitor on your home screen.
Compact battery and data usage widget.
System resources and battery status monitoring widget update
The home screen widget is active and synchronized by the background service.
The widget has not been added to the home screen yet. Long-press the home screen to add it.
Adjust the home screen widget background opacity. 100% is fully opaque.
Pure black instead of the dark blue-grey, in both themes, so the widgets match black neighbours.
Count data usage per calendar day or per one-month billing cycle starting on the selected day. Month lengths are handled automatically.
Set your plan\'s data allowance per counting period; the counter and widget show usage against it and you get a warning at 80 % and at the limit.
Notifies when charging reaches the chosen level, so you can unplug early to protect the battery.
No notifications recorded yet. Logging starts when notification access is granted and new notifications arrive.
No history collected for this metric yet. Daily values appear here as data accumulates.
Everything in this report was read on the device itself. Nothing was sent anywhere.
The search matches any column. Type a date such as 2026-08-14 for one day or 2026-08 for a whole month, or a value such as 12 to find the days with 12 unlocks. Use the date fields for a period.
The search matches any column. Type an app name such as Gmail, a word from the notification title or text, or a date such as 2026-08-14. Use the date fields for a period.
Android counts only metered mobile data. Usage on connections marked as unmetered (e.g. unlimited plans) is not included.
Usage access is required to show data usage.
No charges in the last 14 days
Battery history appears here as the app collects it.
Battery, usage counters and network stats on a home-screen widget, in the app and on a charging screensaver — all read straight from your device, nothing leaves it.
Device Watch only reads what these permissions unlock. Everything keeps working without them — the affected rows just show a dash.
Location and Nearby devices reveal the Wi-Fi network name, Phone shows mobile network details, and Notifications lets the battery-full alert through.
Add the Device Watch widget to your home screen for a live view of battery, memory, CPU, storage and today\'s data usage.
While charging, Device Watch can work as a screensaver: a big clock, charging power in watts, the next alarm and an automatic night dim. Turn it on in the system screensaver settings.
Screen time, unlocks, notifications and data usage are counted per day or per billing cycle, with daily history for the last two months and monthly data totals as far back as Android keeps them.
You can reopen this intro any time from the Settings tab.
Without root, reads through the Shizuku app what Android hides from ordinary apps: the real processor load and the battery\'s own wear figures. Shizuku must be installed and running.
Shizuku is not running. The readings return once you start it.
Shizuku refused the permission. Allow Device Watch in the Shizuku app and try again.
Shizuku is not running. Install Shizuku, start it and try again.

On a rooted phone, reads what Android hides from ordinary apps: the real processor load, chip temperatures and the battery\'s own wear figures. It also opens the Kernel page on the Device tab, with processor profiles. Your root manager asks for permission.
Waiting for your root manager\'s permission…
Root access was refused. Allow Device Watch in your root manager and try again.
Returning the phone\'s own processor speed limits before root goes off…
The processor speed limits set with root stay until the phone restarts: root was no longer there to remove them.
No su command was found. The phone is not rooted, or its root manager (KernelSU, APatch) has not yet been told to allow Device Watch.
The colours and number font from before version 1.6: on Android 12 and newer the colours follow your wallpaper.
Optional alerts for a hot battery, low storage and a fast-draining battery
Let the phone cool down: unplug it and close demanding apps.
%1$s free. The Apps tab lists the largest apps.
The Apps tab shows which apps have been in use.
Off unless you switch them on. Each alert comes once, and again only after things have first returned to normal.
When less than 10 % of the storage is free.
When the battery loses 20 % an hour or more, measured over at least half an hour off the charger.
Charging right now — consumption is shown after unplugging.
No period yet. It starts the next time the battery is charged full or the charger is unplugged.
This period is over a week old — Android keeps detailed usage events for about a week, so the app list may be incomplete.
Android\'s own measurement since the phone last left the charger: %1$s on battery.
This phone does not report how much charge has left the battery, so no amount or pace can be given.
%1$s in %2$s. At this pace a full battery would last about %3$s.
Over %1$s only: too short a stretch to tell a pace.
An ordinary pace for a phone at rest.
More than a phone at rest should use: something keeps it awake. See the list below.
Android\'s estimate of each app\'s share. The screen\'s drain is counted for the app that was open.
With the screen off the phone tries to sleep to save battery. These kept it awake the longest; a high drain at rest usually comes from one of them.
The phone was about to sleep, but something was still under way, so it stayed awake.
The time apps held the phone awake, all together. The apps are in the list above.
The screen was on, so the phone could not sleep.
Sensors were measuring, for step counting or lift-to-wake for example.
Wi-Fi received data or looked for networks.
A Bluetooth device was connected or being looked for.
The mobile network: calls, messages or mobile data.
An app or the system had timed a wake-up: a sync, a reminder or an alarm clock, for example.
Battery monitoring, the charger or a USB connection.
NFC was listening for a tag or a payment terminal.
A touch, a button press or the cover being opened.
Sound was being played or recorded.
The location was being worked out.
The chip maker\'s own identifier for a part of the hardware.
A wake-up the app had timed.
Usage access is required to show screen time for this period.
Notification counting starts when notification access is granted. Ongoing notifications, group summaries and updates to an existing notification are not counted.
Grant usage access so the app can show screen time, app data usage and last-opened dates.
Keep the screensaver upright even when the device is in landscape.
Lower the screen brightness while the screensaver is showing (easier on the eyes overnight).
Show the icons of unread notifications under the clock and pulse them when a new one arrives. Needs notification access.
Notification access is not granted, so the screensaver cannot see notifications. Grant it under Special access below.
The screensaver shifts a little once a minute so nothing burns into the screen. With this on it moves only up and down and stays centred sideways.
Start as soon as charging begins

When charging begins with the screen off, the screensaver comes up even with Always On Display on: at once with extended access, otherwise Device Watch wakes the screen and the screensaver follows in about 10–15 seconds. Nothing happens while the screen is on.
Show the phone\'s name above the clock, as set under About phone in Android\'s settings.
Dim the screensaver automatically between the selected times.

The screensaver is turned on from Android\'s system settings, and it appears when the screen turns off while the device is charging. On some phones (e.g. Samsung) it only starts while charging, and you may need to turn off Always On Display if it shows instead.

This kernel reports no processor speeds.
The faster cores run at most about 60 % of their top speed. Saves battery under heavy use; the little cores stay at full speed.
The faster cores run at most about 80 % of their top speed: nearly all the speed, less heat at the peaks.
The phone\'s own limits: every core may run as fast as the phone itself allows, as before the app changed anything.
Choose each group of cores\' limit yourself, from half its top speed up.
This phone has one group of cores, or all run equally fast: there is no faster group to hold back, so only Custom is offered.
The phone restarted and its own limits came back. Choose the profile again, or switch on Apply after restart too.
Root is not available: the limits set earlier stay until the phone restarts.

Off, the phone\'s own limits return at every restart. On, the profile is set again the first time the screen is on after a restart.

resources.string: With extended access on (Shizuku or root, in Settings) this band shows which apps used the camera, the microphone and the location, and when, from Android\'s own record. Without it, Android\'s own view of the same record is a tap away.
The shell did not answer. Trying again in a moment.
The shell did not answer the last read, so the one before is shown.
This Android keeps no record of camera, microphone and location use; Android 12 and later do.

Android keeps this record itself, for its Privacy dashboard: which app used the camera, the microphone or the location, when, for how long, and whether it was refused. Device Watch reads it through extended access and shows it; nothing here is stored, exported or backed up.
This Android writes no refused attempts down: the record holds only the uses that went ahead.
This Android keeps the record to the minute: uses within one minute count as one, and a length is whole minutes.
On record since %1$s. How far back it reaches is Android\'s choice, usually a few days.
Other things Android counts as private: an accessibility service in use, device identifiers read, and the like.

Apps that asked and were told no: the permission was missing or allowed only while the app is on screen, the camera or microphone switch in Quick Settings was off, or Android never grants that operation to apps at all.
Since the phone started. With the screen off the phone tries to sleep; these are the kernel\'s own counts of what woke it and what held it up.
This kernel does not report its sleep attempts or its wakeup sources.
Root did not answer the last wake read, so the one before is shown.
Apps and system processes could not all be paused in time.
A device could not be readied for sleep.
A device driver refused to power down.
A device failed while waking back up.
Touch counts the time the screen was on: a finger on the glass keeps the phone awake by design.

Remove preinstalled apps you do not use, through extended access. The apps the phone depends on are marked or kept out of reach, every removal is asked about first, and a removed app can be brought back from the same page.

With extended access on (Shizuku or root, in Settings) preinstalled apps you do not use can be removed from here. The apps the phone depends on are marked or kept out of reach, every removal is asked about first, and a removed app can be brought back.

A removal takes the app away from this user only, with its data: the copy on the system image stays, and Restore brings it back, as does a factory reset. Remove only apps you know. A system app can be one that other apps, or the phone itself, rely on; the ones this build knows of say so.
The app is removed for this user and its data cleared. It stays on the system image and can be restored from this page.

the package manager gave no reason
by now it is one the phone cannot do without
it is no longer installed for this user
the package manager called it done, but the app is as it was; a restriction on this user may be the reason
part of Android\'s core; the phone does not start or work without it.
the home screen in use; without it the phone has no launcher. Set another as default first.
a home screen. If it is the only one, the phone is left without a launcher.
the keyboard in use; without it nothing can be typed. Switch to another keyboard first.
a keyboard. If it is the only one, nothing can be typed.
the phone app in use; without it calls, emergency calls included, have no screen.
a phone app. Calls work through another one only if that one is set as default.
the SMS app in use. Text messages stop arriving until another app is set as default.
the web view apps use to show web content and sign-in pages; without it many apps crash.
a web view provider. Keep at least one, or apps that show web content crash.
Google Play services. Most Google apps and many others stop working, and notifications that come through Google stop.
the Play Store. App installs and updates from Google stop.
Bluetooth, NFC or the secure element. That radio stops working, and Settings may crash on its page.
carrier and SIM services. Calls over LTE or Wi-Fi, eSIM or the SIM toolkit may stop.
emergency alerts and emergency information. They stop.
the setup wizard. It is needed after a factory reset, where its absence can leave the phone stuck.
system updates. The phone stops receiving them.
a manufacturer\'s system component. Settings, permissions or app starts may break, and some phones restart in a loop without it.
a chipset vendor\'s component. The radio, camera, audio or location may stop working.
a theme or resource overlay. The look of the system or of an app may break.
the file picker. Attaching files and saving downloads stop working in every app.

The figures you choose are shown in the monitor\'s notification on two lines among your other notifications; expand it to see them all. With none chosen the notification stays silent and folded at the bottom.
Most phones give it only with extended access.
Notifications are off for Device Watch, so the figures are not shown.
One figure of your choice: battery, temperature, data today, uptime, processor, memory or storage.
The figures chosen in Settings, kept up to date while the screen is on.
